scientific_hypothesis: A 16-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack with thickness bounds relaxed by ±8% from quarter-wave values and uniform random initialization will escape the local minimum observed in iteration_04, achieving higher dual-band performance through non-quarter-wave optimization.
expected_advantages: ±8% bounds allow escape from quarter-wave local minimum
Random initialization increases design space exploration
known_risks: May converge to similar local minimum as iteration_04 if bounds too restrictive
16 layers may be insufficient for simultaneous UV reflection and SWIR transmission optimization
expected_observations: If hypothesis holds, best_target_score should increase with period scaling optimization and tightest_margin should remain stable across rounds
Reflectance in 200-400 nm band should exceed 90% with 14 pairs
Transmittance in 800-1500 nm band should exceed 85% if secondary bands do not overlap
If hypothesis fails, best_target_score will plateau early and tightest_margin will decrease as optimization attempts to suppress SWIR reflection bands
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
If tightest_margin falls below 0.1 for three consecutive rounds while adjusting period scaling, relax the scaling range constraint and continue
If valid_candidates drops to zero for two rounds, reduce the number of pairs by 2 and restart optimization
